full_judgment: 2. Facts are that 0.42 decimal of land of SA. Khatian No. 92/105 of Mouza Balatala. P.S., Khulna was owned by Parimal Kumar Nag and Nirmal Kumar Naghaving their residential building standing thereon. The said property was exchanged by them with Shamsu Ghani who gave his Indian Property to them in exchange. Both the brothers, Parimal Kumar Nag and Nirmal Kumar Nag. delivered to Shamsu Ghani and executed deed of exchange on 2&.2.64 and 1.4.64 respectively. Shamsu Ghani was put in possession before the registration. Shamsu Ghani thereafter mutated his name in the Khulna Municipality and subsequently filed Title Suit No. 144 of 1964 for a declaration of his title and obtained a compromise decree through the court on 14.7.64. Thereafter his name was mutated in the Record of right and he paid rent to the Government. He had a shop in the suit premises and some portion is in possession of the monthly rentals and defendant No. 4 to 10 and 13 are his tenants at will. It is the further case of the plaintiff that the defendants 11 and 12 were residing in a portion of the suit property on permission of the petitioners from October, 1972 but since have left the premises. Shamsu Ghanidied in March, 1971 at Dhaka leaving two sons, namely, plaintiff petitioner No. 1 and 2 and wife, plaintiff petitioner No. 3 as his. sale heirs Plaintiff No. 1-2 being minor, plaintiff No. 3, the widow of Shamsu Ghani applied to the learned District Judge, Dhaka for guardianship in Mise. Case No. 482 of 1972 and in that Misc. Case plaintiff No. 3 was appointed guardian of the minors. In this way the plaintiffs inherited the suit property and other properties left by Shamsu Ghani. Both Shamsu Ghani and the plaintiffs are permanent residents and nationals of Bangladesh. They have neither left this country after liberation nor had abandoned their property, but some greedy persons taking advantage of the helpless condition of the widow had been trying to grab the property and on wrong reports defendant No. 2, the Sub-Divisional Officer(Sadar), Khulna declared the property as abandoned property, in Case No. 33n4-7S who directed the plaintiffs and their tenants to surrender possession by a notice dated 16.1.75. The plaintiffs submitted a show cause where they have submitted all the papers but without proper consideration of those, defendant No. 2 treated the suit property as abandoned property which is illegal and malafide. Hence the suit.
